entries.notes: Completed cleanly. Incumbent improved the 8-row iso holdout from 36.712076s to 32.205814s with zero wrong answers, a modest 1.14x aggregate speedup. The profile keeps default preprocessing, disables UF symmetry and eq-bridge, uses theory_phase=polarity, prop_budget=1000, and prop_interval=128. NEQ016 is a real tuned-LLM2SMT gap as well as a Z3 gap: tuned LLM2SMT solves locally in about 21.5s while Primo did not solve before interruption at 92s. The tuned reference did not use LLM2SMT's finite-domain value-precedence option for this improvement; the recorded tuned profile uses UF symmetry, four preprocessing passes, equality bridge, and EUF propagation thresholds.

summary.correctness: Three distinct soundness bugs found and fixed during implementation, all the same root cause (a node's own signature can be rehashed and rediscovered congruent more than once, so naively resolving to 'current identity' and linking through that silently drops a bridge fact from the explanation): (1) ProofForest::explain only alias-resolved the top-level query, not obligations produced mid-walk; (2) re-coalescing an already-aliased member needs its old alias materialized into a real tree edge first, not overwritten; (3) the same applies to the canonical side and to direct-equation endpoints, plus a has_incoming_edge_ tracker was needed since a self-rooted node can already have a real incoming edge a naive parent_[node]==node check would miss. After all three fixes: hand-derived Example 22/23 tests pass, and the 180-step randomized backtracking oracle test passes under both default and ASAN/UBSan builds.

Working hypothesis, not confirmed: materialize()'s retroactive reversals happen outside the normal Union-driven growth pattern Lemma 13's amortized O(log n) bound depends on ('each reversal at least doubles the reversed edge's tree size'), and may violate that invariant. Not investigated further this session.

summary.bug: has_incoming_edge_ (added to gate ProofForest::coalesce_into_structural_class's cheap alias fast path, see the previous run's fix 3) only covered real union_nodes e_prime targets, not coalesce_into_structural_class's own fast-path alias targets. summary.profile_finding: perf record on NEQ016_size7 (20s bounded window, process did not terminate pre-fix) showed ~76% of all samples inside ProofForest::explain and its two NCA-search helpers: aux_find 38%, explain 19%, nearest_common_ancestor 13%, explain_along_path 6%. Every other function, including all of FlatCongruenceClosure's own merge/backtrack machinery, was individually under 0.1%. This is the inverse of every other mode's profile.
summary.bug_1_tree_depth: Lemma 13's amortized O(log n) reversal bound requires every Union to reverse the smaller side's path. reoriented-proof-forest's direct-equation caller already does this (chooses e/e' by live class_size_ before calling union_nodes). coalesce_into_structural_class's fallback branch (member vs canonical, chosen by lookup-table arrival order) and materialize (always reverses the alias source's path) had no size discipline at all, and live class_size_ stops being an accurate proxy for real tree size once fast-path aliasing exists (an aliased member inflates its live class without adding real tree depth). Fixed by adding ProofForest's own size_ tracking and making union_nodes itself swap which physical node plays e vs e' when the caller's choice disagrees with tracked size -- sound regardless of caller intent, since a tree edge's label proves its two endpoints equal however it is attached. Verified via direct instrumentation: max real tree depth stayed at 46 after 200,000 union_nodes calls post-fix, versus growing unboundedly before.
summary.bug_2_memoization: Fixing bug 1 alone did not fix NEQ016_size7 (still did not finish in 30s). Further instrumentation showed seed_and_resolve (explain's alias-chain walker) called over 1 billion times in 15 seconds against only ~5,000 top-level Explain calls in that window; alias-chain hop count itself stayed flat (max 1 hop, confirming bug 1's fix was working and this was a separate issue). The auxiliary union-find already deduplicates repeat tree-edge congruence obligations reached via explain_along_path's NCA walk (the mechanism Section 5.2's own complexity argument depends on), but nothing deduplicated repeat alias-bridge obligations reached via seed_and_resolve -- a coalesced node's bridge obligations were pushed once per referencing obligation, not once per Explain call, and structural-class coalescing routinely produces a few popular hub canonical nodes referenced many times within one call. Fixed with the same generation-stamped mark pattern already used for aux_generation_/ancestor_generation_ in this file (seed_marks_/seed_generation_): a node's bridge obligations are now pushed at most once per top-level Explain call.
summary.result: NEQ016_size7 standalone: 180s+ (not finishing) -> 3.67s, in line with default (3.11s) and reoriented-proof-forest (3.05s). 334-file sweep (10s timeout): solved 232->248 (PAR2 9.329->8.643); reoriented-proof-forest in the same post-fix run was 254/8.279, so the gap closed from 27 files behind to 6 files behind, and file-level divergence dropped from 43/334 to 20/334. Not yet a clear win over reoriented-proof-forest, but no longer a clear, broad loss.
summary.verification: Unit tests and a freshly-configured ASAN/UBSan build pass after each of the two fixes. A 2000-instance fuzzsmt-against-z3 round against the ASAN/UBSan build came back 2000/2000 PASS after each fix (0 crashes, 0 disagreements) -- confirms neither fix introduced a new soundness issue, including the size-based e/e' swap in union_nodes, which changes the internal tree shape for every mode sharing that function (reoriented-proof-forest included) but was argued sound because a tree edge's label does not depend on which physical node carries it; the existing full test suite (including reoriented-proof-forest's own tests) still passes unchanged.

summary.round1_pre_fix: 300 cases: 257 UNSUPPORTED_INPUT (sat refs), 38 UNSUPPORTED_INPUT (unsat refs), 5 CRASH, 0 PASS. Nearly universal UNSUPPORTED_INPUT traced to a real bug: build_times/build_divide recognized a literal `*`/`/` operand by pattern-matching the raw S-expression before ever calling build_term, so a let-bound alias of a literal (e.g. `(let ((c 3)) (* c x))`) was never recognized as a coefficient, even though it resolves to one after build_term's own let-binding lookup. fuzzsmt let-binds nearly every literal in its QF_LRA output, so this rejected almost all fuzzer-generated input.
summary.fix: Rewrote build_times/build_divide to build both operands via build_term first (which already resolves let-bindings, definitions, and nested arithmetic that constant-folds via TermManager's own mk_plus/mk_times), then check the *resulting* term's TermKind::Rational-ness -- simpler than the original raw-syntax-matching design, not just more correct. The top-level bare-numeral-atom fast path was also simplified to a plain util::Rational::parse(expr.atom) check inside build_term's Atom branch, since compound literal forms (`(- lit)`, `(/ lit n)`) are now handled correctly by the ordinary build_minus/build_divide recursive-build path with no special-casing needed.
summary.round2_post_fix: Same 300-case campaign re-run after the fix: 251 UNSUPPORTED_INPUT (sat refs), 17 UNSUPPORTED_INPUT (unsat refs), 20 PASS (unsat/unsat), 3 PASS (sat/sat), 6 CRASH, 3 TIMEOUT (5s budget). Zero wrong-answer disagreements against z3 across both rounds -- the critical soundness property held throughout.
summary.crash_triage: All 6 crashes share one signature: AddressSanitizer stack-overflow inside primo::smtlib::SExpr's recursive copy constructor, triggered purely by S-expression nesting depth, before any theory-specific code runs. Confirmed NOT QF_LRA-specific: reproduced the same fuzzer settings against QF_UF (100 cases) with zero crashes, but QF_UF's fuzzsmt output at these settings averaged ~136 lines/file versus QF_LRA's ~534 lines/file (fuzzsmt's arithmetic term generator produces deeper nesting) -- QF_LRA just happens to hit the same latent, pre-existing, theory-agnostic parser-robustness gap more often, not a new one. Out of scope for this milestone; tracked as a follow-up (would need converting SExpr copying and/or build_term's recursion to be iterative, or adding an explicit depth limit).
summary.remaining_unsupported_input: Manually sampled several post-fix UNSUPPORTED_INPUT cases: overwhelmingly the known, explicitly-tested disequality gap ("QF_LRA disequality (a negated Real equality) is not yet supported") -- fuzzsmt generates many equalities that end up negated somewhere in the formula. This is an intentional, documented Milestone 1 scope boundary (case-splitting for disequality isn't implemented yet), not an unknown bug.

summary.result: First run (before the bug fix below): 255 PASS, 16 TIMEOUT, 229 CRASH -- a real regression, all crashes the SAME new bug (CaDiCaL abort 'external reason clause must contain the propagated literal'), not the pre-existing SExpr recursion issue. Root cause: OnlineLraPropagator::notify_backtrack cleared its entire reasons_ map unconditionally on every backtrack, including entries for literals that remained assigned after backtracking to new_level -- CaDiCaL's conflict analysis (explain_external_propagations) legitimately asked for such a literal's reason later and got an empty clause back. Fixed by only erasing a reasons_ entry when its literal's var is actually popped from the propagator's own var_trail_ (mirroring how assigned_ is already scoped), leaving pending_ (undelivered candidates only, always safe to drop) as the sole thing cleared unconditionally. Re-ran the same 500-case campaign after the fix: 424 PASS, 69 TIMEOUT, 7 CRASH, 0 WRONG -- all 7 crashes individually reconfirmed (via direct stack-trace inspection) as the identical pre-existing SExpr stack-overflow already triaged in the Milestone 1 entry, not a new issue.
summary.significance: This is the second real bug (after the let-bound-literal and real-equality-misclassification bugs in Milestone 1) caught by the project's fuzz-gate discipline rather than shipped -- a subtle backtracking/reason-clause-lifetime bug that unit tests alone (which don't exercise deep, varied DPLL(T) backtracking patterns) would have been very unlikely to catch. Reinforces that the merge-gate tier (500 cases) is pulling real weight for propagator-touching changes, exactly as it did for Milestone 3a.

summary.result: Two bugs found and fixed in sequence, each caught before landing cleanly: (1) SExpr's recursive copy ctor/destructor and parser.cpp's recursive parse_one both replaced with iterative algorithms (Frame-stack based) -- fixed all 7 crashes from the prior Milestone 3b fuzz-gate entry (confirmed: same corpus files, re-run after this fix alone, all 7 stopped crashing). (2) Frontend::build_term's own recursive descent turned out to be a SEPARATE, deeper bug: even with SExpr fixed, a synthetic 200000-deep nested `+` still segfaulted (Release build) via TermManager::mk_plus's call chain through build_term/build_ite/etc, and ASAN's larger stack frames meant it was actually THIS bug, not the SExpr one, causing all 7 of the Milestone 3b fuzz-gate crashes under ASAN. Fixed via TermBuilder, a continuation-passing iterative driver. Caught a genuine design mistake in the first TermBuilder attempt during local testing (before it ever reached fuzzing): only child-descent was trampolined, not continuation delivery, so long chains still recursed natively via direct k(...) calls -- fixed by routing every continuation invocation through resume() too. Local verification (500 QF_LRA + 300 QF_UF fuzzsmt cases, ASAN/UBSan): 0 crashes, 0 wrong answers, both up from a 7/500 crash rate before the fix. A campaign-tier (3000+ case) QF_LRA fuzz gate was additionally submitted to the llm2smt-slurm cluster (job 113267) for independent confirmation at scale, per standing project guidance that campaign-tier fuzzing belongs on Slurm rather than run locally.
summary.significance: Removes a theory-agnostic crash class that had been present (and repeatedly rediscovered/re-triaged as 'pre-existing, out of scope') since Milestone 1's fuzz gate. summary.result: Two real infrastructure bugs found and fixed while getting this campaign running (neither is a Primo correctness issue): (1) the first submission (job 113267, against the pre-M4 commit) completed in ~1 second with 'fuzzsmt is not installed; skipping external fuzzing' -- slurm_prepare_benchmark_workspace.py only builds the primo binary, not the fuzzsmt/z3 tooling scripts/fuzz_external.py depends on, so that job silently did nothing rather than actually fuzzing. Fixed by running `make contrib-fuzzsmt contrib-z3` remotely and setting up a .venv-yinyang venv with yinyang/z3-solver installed for opfuzz/typefuzz. (2) The very next slurm_prepare_benchmark_workspace.py sync (to pick up the M4 commits) then clobbered that remote contrib/local with the LOCAL machine's contrib/local via rsync (contrib/local wasn't excluded), reintroducing the same failure via a different symptom (fuzzsmt's wrapper script has a host-specific absolute jarfile path baked in at install time) -- fixed by excluding contrib/local and contrib/src from the rsync (commit 605caad), then re-provisioning remotely. A remaining minor PATH gap (opfuzz specifically resolves via bare PATH lookup, not the TYPEFUZZ override) was caught and fixed with a small supplementary single-task job (113328) rather than restarting the whole array. As of this entry, job 113319's core fuzzsmt shards (0-5) are running (confirmed genuinely executing, not instantly completing); yinyang shards (7-8) already completed cleanly (14/14 seeds valid, 0 bug triggers); opfuzz (113328) is running. summary.result: Solved (of 237): primo 102 (43%), z3 167 (70%), cvc5 150 (63%). PAR2 (10s timeout): primo 2799, z3 1531, cvc5 1885. Zero 3-way disagreements on concrete sat/unsat answers across all 237 files -- Primo's answers, where it produces one, are never wrong relative to either reference solver. Per-family breakdown is NOT uniform: Primo fully matches z3/cvc5 (15/15 or 2/2) on keymaera, meti-tarski, sal, spider_benchmarks, check, and is close on DTP-Scheduling (11 vs 15/13); on 2017-Heizmann-UltimateInvariantSynthesis, LassoRanker, and tropical-matrix all three solvers struggle roughly equally (these are genuinely hard for everyone, matching earlier quick-eval findings). But on TM (4 vs 15/14), sc (4 vs 13/12), uart (3 vs 13/12), 2019-ezsmt (3 vs 10/7), tta_startup (8 vs 14/13), and miplib (1 vs 6/5), Primo is specifically and substantially behind while z3/cvc5 mostly solve these within the same 10s budget. summary.significance: First genuine empirical evidence of WHERE Primo is behind, rather than inferring from a 17-file one-per-family sample dominated by the 'hard for everyone' families. This broader, family-stratified sample reveals a *different*, more tractable-looking set of gap families (TM, sc, uart, 2019-ezsmt, tta_startup, miplib) that the earlier narrow sample never surfaced -- these are prime candidates for follow-up investigation (e.g. profiling what's actually slow on a representative TM/uart timeout case) before further committing to items 2/3/4's engineering directions, since none of those (row-based propagation, SOI-Simplex) were evaluated against this specific, more informative family set.

Concentrated in TM (9), uart (9), sc (8), 2019-ezsmt (7), latendresse (6), miplib (5), tta_startup (5), DTP-Scheduling (4), clock_synchro (4), Heizmann/LassoRanker (3). Fastest reference times are 0.13-0.57s on most of them. Families where Primo already ties both references (keymaera, meti-tarski, sal, spider_benchmarks, check) and where all three fail (tropical-matrix) are excluded as design targets.
summary.three_bottleneck_classes: Class A (latendresse): 0 decisions, 1 check() call -- one conjunctive LP that never finishes, so SAT-side heuristics are irrelevant there. Class B (clock_synchro 1,515 decisions / 8,997 pivots / 13.9s; miplib pp08a-12000 4,564 / 8,314 / 13.9s): ~1.5 ms per pivot. Class C (DTP-Scheduling constraints-tempo-width-30: 60,750 decisions, ZERO conflicts, 63,021 check calls, 7,182 pivots, 19.5s): ~320 microseconds per decision with no learning at all.
summary.perf_flat_profile: On constraints-tempo-width-30: LraTableau::pivot 31.4% self; allocator ~42% (_int_malloc 10.5, _int_free 7.9, malloc 5.8, cfree 5.2, malloc_consolidate 5.2, unlink_chunk 4.3, gmp_default_allocate 1.5); GMP copy/init ~12% (__gmpn_copyi 5.6, __gmpz_init_set 3.4, __gmpq_clear 1.6); actual bignum arithmetic ~5% (__gmpz_mul 1.4, __gmpq_mul 1.0, __gmpz_gcd 0.8, __gmpn_gcd_1 0.7, __gmpz_divexact_gcd 0.5, __gmpq_aors 0.5); rebuild_occurs_in_index 1.3%.
summary.corrects_prior_conclusion: This contradicts the conclusion recorded under roadmap item 0's follow-up (2026-07-26) that what remained after the container fixes was inherent mpq_class GCD canonicalization that 'no container-level fix can remove'. Measured, canonicalization/GCD is under 2% and ALL real bignum arithmetic is ~5%; ~54% is malloc/free plus copying of TINY numbers. The values are small, the representation is expensive -- which makes a small-rational (int64/int64 with GMP fallback) fast path the single largest available lever, not a dead end.
summary.tableau_shape: Share of prepared rows that are a single-variable slack (row = c*x): latendresse/ecoliFBAyicesTest-500 3,161/4,555 (69%); TM/p6-zenonumeric_s5 1,311/1,378 (95%); miplib/pp08a-12000 262/400 (66%); sc-17 462/1,185 (39%); uart-17 526/1,446 (36%); tta_startup 84/584 (14%); LassoRanker/selectSort 653/9,469 (7%); clock_synchro 5/264 (2%); DTP-Scheduling/constraints-tempo-width-30 0/3,932 (0%, average row exactly 2.00 and max row 2 -- a pure difference-logic problem in QF_LRA clothing). Dutertre & de Moura Section 2 introduces slack variables only for compound polynomials; Primo allocates one per distinct polynomial including bare variables, and because polynomial keys are exact-content matches, '(<= 0 r1)' and '(<= r1 1000)' land on two DIFFERENT slacks for the same variable.
summary.fill_in: Rows densify 3-5x during search. constraints-tempo-width-30: average row 2.00 -> 3.7-8.9, max row 33, max occurs_in 2,127. clocksynchro_2clocks: 2.75 -> 8.1-14.3, max row 34, max occurs_in 174. ecoliFBAyicesTest-500: 3.39 -> 7.9-23.9, max row 961, and fewer than 2,000 pivots in 30+s (>15 ms per pivot). Since pivot() costs |occurs_in(entering)| * |row(leaving)| rational operations, and none of Bland/Dantzig/SOI prices a pivot by its cost, fill-in is currently unopposed.
summary.design_output: docs/qf-lra-heuristics.md proposes six items in priority order: H2 small-rational fast path in util::Rational; H1 direct bounds for single-variable atoms plus scale-canonical polynomial keys (which subsumes not-yet-scheduled roadmap item 3 and removes item 7's documented single_variable_slack positive-coefficient quirk); H3 fill-in-aware Markowitz-style entering-variable selection with a prefer-|coeff|=1 tie-break and partial pricing; H5 model-based phase selection via CaDiCaL's phase()/unphase() to keep item 8's win without its VSIDS-override regressions; H4 batched bound assertion deferring update() to item 6's existing quiescence point; H6 difference-logic fragment detection (Tier 1) with Cotton & Maler DL0-DL4 as the larger Tier 2. Recommended order: H2 -> H1 -> H3 -> H5 -> H4 -> H6.

summary.bug_found_during_implementation: The debug/ASAN-only check_invariant() caught a real disagreement between from_mpq's 'fits small' test (mpz_fits_slong_p, which admits INT64_MIN) and the small form's own range (which excludes INT64_MIN so negation can never overflow). The two differed by exactly that one value, which would have produced a big-form value that also fit the small form -- two representations for one number, hashing two ways, silently breaking PolynomialKey hash-consing rather than giving a wrong answer. Fixed by giving both a single shared predicate. Separately, a deliberate-mutation check (disabling demotion) confirmed the unit tests fail loudly when the invariant is broken.

benchmark.suite: Six instances spanning both cases: five whose coefficients never leave 32 bits, and clock_synchro/clocksynchro_2clocks, which does overflow

summary.result: 64-bit kept. TM/p5-zenonumeric_s5 0.13s vs 0.13s (1.00x), sc-21.induction3 1.56 vs 1.55 (1.01x), uart-18.induction 0.57 vs 0.53 (1.08x), miplib/pp08a-12000 1.48 vs 1.59 (0.93x), DTP-Scheduling/constraints-tempo-width-30 7.59 vs 8.77 (0.87x) -- all five with ZERO promotions under both widths. clock_synchro/clocksynchro_2clocks 2.44s (32-bit) vs 1.10s (64-bit), 2.22x, with promotions 668,002 vs 358,801 and big-form operations 4,435,074 vs 364,834.
summary.interpretation: The trade-off is exactly the one predicted when the deviation was documented, now measured. Where coefficients stay small the widths are within noise or 32-bit is up to ~13% faster, because __int128 add/multiply are multi-instruction sequences where 64-bit ones are single instructions -- a cost paid on every operation. Where coefficients genuinely outgrow 32 bits, the wider fast path cuts big-form operations 12-fold and wins by 2.2x. A few percent on the common case buys a factor of two on the hard case.
summary.bug_found: Building the 32-bit variant immediately failed the existing representation_transitions unit test: Rational(std::int64_t) range-checked only `value >= -kSmallMax`, which is vacuous at kSmallMax == INT64_MAX (every std::int64_t satisfies it) but lets out-of-range values into the small form at any narrower width, violating the canonical-form invariant. Fixed in commit 251d29e. A latent bug in a knob nobody had turned yet.

verification.both_widths_tested: Release ctest 12/12 at both widths after the fix; ASAN/UBSan 12/12 at the shipped 64-bit width.
verification.scope: Local design-decision evidence, explicitly not a benchmark claim -- no Slurm run was made for the 32-bit variant, and none is warranted since it is not being shipped.

entries.scope: docs/qf-lra-heuristics.md item H3: fill-in-aware entering-variable selection (PivotingRule::Sparse, commit cf491ce) and its promotion to the default together with the leaving-side half (commit dd60655). Includes the four-way 237-file promotion run that also settles item H1b, and the merge/campaign fuzz gates. pivot() rewrites every row in occurs_in_[entering] merging in a row of length |row(leaving)|, so a pivot's cost and the fill-in it creates are the Markowitz product of those two factors -- which none of Bland, Dantzig or SOI prices. Source: Monniaux (CAV 2009) p.8; only that sparsity criterion is taken from the paper.

entries.scope: Investigation of four truncated fuzz-gate shards during the milestone-wide campaign sweep (jobs 117248-117251), and the correction of a wrong first diagnosis. Recorded because the failure pattern looked exactly like a solver termination bug and was not one -- the next person to see a whole-shard timeout should not have to re-derive this.

environment.host: llm2smt-slurm; compute partition 9/9 allocated with 460+ jobs queued from other users during the failures

command.original: scripts/slurm_qfuf_fuzz_gate.sbatch, 6 fuzzsmt shards x 500 cases per configuration, --time=00:45:00
command.reruns: same shards resubmitted with --time=03:00:00 (jobs 117309-117312) and again at --time=02:00:00 (117333-117336)
command.isolation: srun on a compute node running fuzz_external.py directly with python3 -u, once writing to node-local /tmp and once to the same NFS fuzz-results tree the gate uses; plus the generator alone, and per-case timing/peak-RSS sweeps locally and remotely

summary.symptom: Four of the five sweep configurations reported 2500 of 3000 fuzzsmt cases, all otherwise clean (0 crashes, 0 wrong answers). One shard per job had hit the Slurm wall clock and been killed before fuzz_external.py writes summary.csv, so the shard vanished from the results rather than failing -- a truncated gate is indistinguishable from a clean one unless the summary count is checked.
summary.what_made_it_look_like_a_solver_bug: All four lost shards were the same FuzzSMT seed, 217251, across four DIFFERENT solver configurations (bland, dantzig, --no-lra-sparse-leaving, --no-lra-propagation), while the fifth job (row propagation), whose seed range skips 217251, completed every shard. It reproduced on a second run at a 3x longer wall limit, which produced zero case lines in three hours.
summary.why_it_is_not: The same seed completes 500/500 everywhere it was retried: locally in ~40s; on a compute node writing to node-local /tmp; and on a compute node writing to the same NFS fuzz-results tree the gate uses, in 126 seconds. Generation of its 500 files takes 0.33s locally and 0.61s remotely. Peak RSS across its cases is ~95MB for Primo and ~153MB for z3, against the 2G cgroup. Both the solver and the reference calls are already timeout-bounded at 5s inside fuzz_external.py, so a shard cannot exceed roughly COUNT * 2 * TIMEOUT = 83 minutes of solving -- the failures ran 180.
summary.conclusion: No solver hang. An environment/scheduling anomaly during a period when the cluster was saturated by other users' work; it did not reproduce once the queue drained. The cluster nodes are also 3-5x slower per case than the workstation (5 of the seed's cases exceed 8s remotely where only 1 hits the 5s cap locally), which narrows the margin but does not come close to explaining 180 minutes.
summary.corrected_diagnosis: An earlier commit (2b6e197) asserted the 45-minute limit was under the worst case 'by construction' and implied that was the cause. The arithmetic is right and the raise to two hours is kept as defence in depth, but it was NOT the cause here -- 83 minutes does not explain a 180-minute failure, and the shard actually completes in about two. The script comment has been corrected rather than left confidently wrong.

Includes the profiling pass that located the remaining gap.

summary.headline: Solved of 595: z3 429 (72.1%), primo 373 (62.7%), cvc5 351 (59.0%). PAR2: z3 23138s, primo 29215s, cvc5 31766s. Primo beats cvc5 by 22 files and trails z3 by 56. ZERO cross-solver disagreements, zero crashes, zero errors, zero unsupported across all 595 files in all three solvers.
summary.correction_to_earlier_claims: On the 237-file stratified sample Primo had edged z3 168-167. That does NOT hold on an unseen set. The stratified sample -- assembled during this roadmap and used as its promotion bar -- was optimistic, which is exactly why the scrambled set was worth running.
summary.soundness_caveat: Scrambled benchmarks carry no (set-info :status), so bench_qf_uf_full.py's own wrong-answer column is inert here: it derives `expected` from :status and reports wrong=false for every row regardless of the answer. The zero-disagreement result above comes from scripts/compare_solver_answers.py comparing the three solvers against each other, which is the only soundness signal this set supports.
summary.gap_is_one_size_band: Solved by file size (primo / z3 / cvc5): 0-50KB 180/181/181 of 182; 50-500KB 142/134/122 of 191; 500KB-5MB 43/100/43 of 173; >5MB 8/14/5 of 49. Primo LEADS both references below 500KB and collapses above it, landing on exactly cvc5's number in the 500KB-5MB band. 18 files are solved only by Primo, 60 only by z3, 0 only by cvc5; 146 by nobody.
summary.not_a_preprocessing_size_problem: First hypothesis, and refuted by measurement. On four profiled gap instances Primo's prepared tableau matches z3's reported dimensions within ~5%: 9,315x11,633 vs 9,000x11,330; 8,960x10,479 vs 8,892x10,415; 4,822x5,405 vs 4,342x4,929; 24,976x27,016 vs 22,792x26,486. Primo also already folds the scrambler's (* 1.0 t)/(+ t 0.0) obfuscation -- verified directly, term size and solve-eqs counts identical with and without it. Both solvers build the same problem.
summary.diagnosis: The instances are dominated by Real equalities (8,226-40,820 lowered per file against 4,822-24,976 rows). Primo lowers t1=t2 to a pair of inequalities that item H1b puts on one shared slack, which then holds an upper and a lower bound at the same value -- a FIXED variable that Primo never exploits, leaving it a live pivotable row. z3 does exploit it: :arith-fixed-eqs 168-52,364 and :arith-offset-eqs 855-68,937 per instance, after which its search barely runs. On scrambled126657 z3 needs 9 decisions and 4 conflicts where Primo makes 141,124 decisions and 321M pivot term-operations. perf puts 86% of Primo's runtime in LraTableau::pivot, averaging 431 rows rewritten per pivot.
summary.timeout_caveat: z3's median time on the 76 files it wins and Primo loses is 25s of the 60s budget (max 57.9s), so it is near the boundary too. At 60s a 2x slower solver loses many files a longer budget would recover, and the competition's own timeout is 1200s -- this run may overstate the gap under competition conditions. Job 117414 re-runs exactly those 76 files at 600s to separate 'cannot' from 'needs more budget'.

entries.scope: docs/qf-lra-heuristics.md item H7: fixed-variable elimination. A basic variable whose bounds coincide is pivoted out of the basis, since can_enter() already makes a fixed NON-basic variable inert while a fixed basic one demands a repair pivot whenever any term in its row moves. Designed from the 2026-07-29 scrambled-competition profiling, which found these instances dominated by lowered Real equalities that item H1b puts on one shared slack. NOT PROMOTED: it did not clear the 595-file bar and ships opt-in behind --lra-fixed-elimination. Its row-freezing half was deleted outright.

summary.headline: H7 does not clear its bar. Scrambled 595 at 60s: 373 solved with it off, 374 on, 375 with the freezing half disabled. PAR2 29204 / 29237 / 29195. Net +1 file on 595 with +19/-18 symmetric churn. Stratified 237 at 10s: 167 -> 168, PAR2 1559.1 -> 1531.7. Zero cross-solver disagreements on either set.
summary.the_mechanism_does_work: Local paired A/B is unambiguous per-instance: latendresse/ecoliFBAyicesTest-500 0.8s -> 0.1s (:lra.pivot-term-ops 8.66M -> 0.13M), scrambled335326 51.0s -> 14.9s (195M -> 27M), and roughly an order of magnitude less pivot work on instances that still time out. The diagnosis that these tableaus are dominated by fixed equality slacks is correct.
summary.but_it_is_bimodal: It does not generalize, and the band breakdown is what shows it. Solved by file size (H7-off / H7-on-without-freezing / z3): 0-50KB 177/179/178 of 179; 50-500KB 144/138/136 of 192; 500KB-5MB 45/45/101 of 174; >5MB 7/13/14 of 50. Per-band gain/loss for H7: 0-50KB +2/-0, 50-500KB +2/-8, 500KB-5MB +8/-8, >5MB +8/-2.
summary.where_the_gap_actually_is: The ENTIRE remaining 56-file deficit against z3 is the 500KB-5MB band (45 vs 101). H7 nets exactly zero there. Over the 32 files in that band both configurations solve in more than a second the MEDIAN is 0.64x -- the typical gap instance is 1.6x SLOWER -- with 17 files >20% slower against 8 files >25% faster. Overall median across all commonly-solved files is 0.94x.
summary.real_win_where_it_is_not_needed: The >5MB band is the one genuine gain: 7 -> 13 of 50, +8 gained against -2 lost, closing a 7-file deficit against z3's 14 down to 1. Among the 5 files both configurations solve there the median is 0.98x, so the gains are files crossing the 60s line rather than a broad speedup.
summary.methodological_correction: The four instances profiled to design H7 were all in the 500KB-5MB band, so the band choice was right -- but they were the winning tail of it, not a representative sample, and three of the four still timed out with H7 enabled. Presenting their 3.4x/8x as evidence the mechanism 'works' over-generalized from an instance selection biased toward the hypothesis under test. The band-level median (0.64x) is what caught it. Future gap work should profile the MEDIAN instance of the target band.
summary.freezing_deleted: The row-freezing half (drop a qualifying row from occurs_in_ so update()/check() skip it) was strictly negative: four files lost in the 500KB-5MB band against one gained elsewhere. It also carried all of H7's wrong-answer risk -- mark_boundable's caller contract, the throw enforcing it, the stale-assignment argument, the frozen-row-whose-term-later-became-basic case, RowDeactivationTrailEntry. Removed outright rather than left behind a flag: 352 lines deleted against 106 added (ebd2533). What remains has no wrong-answer mode; it is a pivot, which is what check() does on every repair.
summary.no_threshold_added: Deliberately did NOT add a size or row-length threshold to keep the >5MB win while dodging the mid-range cost. That is tuning a heuristic that lost its own bar -- item 8's recorded mistake.
summary.what_this_says_about_the_gap: The fixed-equality hypothesis is now tested and largely refuted for the band that holds the deficit. That is worth more than the +1 file: it removes the most plausible remaining explanation. Offset equalities (z3's :arith-offset-eqs, 855-68,937 per instance) remain untested.

verification.ablation_invariance: With H7 off, :sat.decisions and :lra.pivots are byte-identical to the pre-H7 build on the six-instance counter probe -- checked at eed259c and again after the demotion, so the shipped default is exactly pre-H7 behaviour.
verification.tests: Release and ASAN ctest green throughout. Unit tests pin: the elimination fires; the unbounded-candidate preference; that an already-fixed candidate is never pivoted INTO the basis (that guard was a real bug -- the other ranking criteria actively steer into picking one, and the test fails without it); conflict still found through an eliminated variable with every certificate literal genuinely asserted; push/pop across an elimination; verdict agreement with the ablation under both pivoting rules.
verification.mutation_checks: Before its removal, the freezing guard was mutation-checked both ways. Dropping it entirely made an existing end-to-end test return the wrong verdict (gaussian_elimination_can_be_disabled). Dropping only the mark_boundable half fired the throw immediately on real benchmarks (variable 1133 on scrambled335326, 1584 on ecoliFBAyicesTest-500). Both confirm the guard was load-bearing, which is why removing the feature it guarded was preferable to keeping both.
verification.fuzzing: 2100 fuzzsmt cases against z3 under ASAN with H7 enabled (300+300+1500, zero mismatches, timeouts only), plus an ASAN differential against the ablation over all 237 stratified files and the 60 smallest scrambled files: 0 sanitizer hits, 0 verdict mismatches. A further 1500-case ASAN campaign against z3 covers the shipped opt-in path specifically (--lra-fixed-elimination, freezing removed), since the earlier 2100 ran when H7 was default-on WITH freezing: 1428 PASS / 72 TIMEOUT, zero mismatches.
verification.invalid_gate: Job 117585 reported COMPLETED and had run ZERO cases: its only summary row was SKIPPED_MISSING_FUZZER. The gate script never put contrib/local/bin on PATH, relying on --export=ALL to inherit it from the submitting shell -- which works from an interactive shell but not from `ssh host bash -s` -- and fuzz_external.py treats a missing fuzzer as a skip with exit 0. Both fixed in 0524733 (PATH set inside the job; missing fuzzsmt/z3 now exits 2). Resubmitted as 117589. Recorded because a green job that tested nothing is the same class of error as the truncated shards of 117248-117251.
verification.merge_gate: Job 117589, the opt-in path (--lra-fixed-elimination) against build-slurm-rel: 1000 fuzzsmt QF_LRA cases over two shards, 997 PASS / 3 TIMEOUT, zero wrong answers against z3. Summary row counts checked against the 500-per-shard expectation before believing it, which is what caught 117585.
